title: A steeper line means what?
hook: Two journeys reach the same distance in different times.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Slope is distance change divided by time change. Both lines reach 12 km, but the steeper one reaches it in half the time: 12 rather than 6 km/h.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Slope is distance change divided by time change. Both lines reach 12 km, but the steeper one reaches it in half the time: 12 rather than 6 km/h.

claims.text: Slope is distance change divided by time change. Both lines reach 12 km, but the steeper one reaches it in half the time: 12 rather than 6 km/h. A straight distance–time line represents constant speed over the interval.
claims.source: For a straight distance-time graph, slope = delta distance / delta time. 12/2=6 and 12/1=12 km/h.

recall.question: A straight distance–time graph rises 30 km over 3 hours. What is its slope?
recall.why: 30 km divided by 3 h is 10 km/h.
